headline: Race-week-minus kept quiet; shoes tested, body clean
narrative: A proper race-week-minus, mostly. Monday was race-pack pick-up by bike, Tuesday a short run with strides, and midweek stayed to walks and weights. The real decision was footwear: new shoes bought Thursday — a risky move this close — then taken up Sierra Helada twice on Friday for a test drive. Verdict positive, though a touch less grippy on rock than the old pair, so the weather may pick the shoe on the night. Saturday was a short flat leg-stretcher, Sunday an easy ride and race plotting over a Guinness. That Friday double nudged vert a shade over a target meant as a ceiling — a small surplus, six days out, forgivable.

The body report is the one that matters now, and it is clean: no flags all week — nothing from the descent-watch right quad on the Sierra Helada drops, nothing from the adductor, calf or ankle. The build to Costa Blanca is done; nothing this week changed fitness, and nothing broke. Race week asks for almost nothing: travel, a short shakeout, the Friday-afternoon nap, and fuel. GTCB goes off Friday night at eleven.
